title: Sociocultural knowledge is needed for selection of shots in hate speech detection tasks
measurement_description: The paper measures how hate speech detection models rely on religious identity terms (e.g., 'Muslim', 'Juden') for making predictions. It evaluates whether models erroneously associate these terms with hateful content, leading to bias and potential over-filtering of text mentioning religious groups.
findings: Hate speech detection models rely heavily on religious target group names (e.g., 'Muslims', 'Juden', 'Mohammedaner') to make predictions. This over-reliance can lead to an erroneous association between the mere mention of a religious group and hate speech, potentially causing the marginalization of these groups by misclassifying and filtering out innocuous content.
